text: How should the headless harness run?

options.label: A command-line tool (npm run sim) bundled by Vite, running games across worker threads and writing JSON, CSV, and an HTML report
options.rationale: No new dependency, same module resolution as the app, and reports that can be compared run to run.

options.label: The same command-line tool run through tsx, with no build step
Inside Vitest only, with seeds split across several soak files
Drop this idea or defer it

text: Which run sizes should be standard?

options.label: 200 games in every npm test (as today), 1000 games on demand with npm run sim
options.rationale: 200 games (about 103 decided) catch large imbalances (a 13 percent share of decided games spans 8 to 21 percent); 1000 games narrow it to about +/- 3 points and take seconds.

options.label: Only 10-game smoke runs in npm test; 200 and 1000 on demand
1000 games in every npm test

text: Which metrics must the first harness report carry? Choose all that apply.

options.label: Recommended set: win share per faction with 95 percent intervals, decided and freeze rates, game-length distribution, battles per turn and results by odds column, losses per faction, first-turn moves
options.rationale: Answers the open balance questions (freezes, the Southern command) and checks the combat table behaves as designed.

options.label: Per-territory capture counts for a map heat view
Economy per faction per turn (income, spending, stockpile, recruits), once the economy exists
Computer-player behaviour: share of armies that never move, offensives started and abandoned

text: Should harness results fail the build?

options.label: Keep today's guards (no early wins, no abandonments, determinism) as failures; report balance numbers with intervals without failing
options.rationale: Balance moves with every rule change; failing the build on it would force tuning loops the owner ruled out (P3).

options.label: Also fail the build when the freeze rate exceeds its budget
Fail the build on any faction's share leaving a target band
Never fail the build on the soak; report only

text: How should we compare rule variants (A/B)?

options.label: Variants are small JSON patches over the scenario (for example digging-in cap 2), run on the same seeds as the baseline, with the difference and its interval reported
options.rationale: Paired seeds cut dice noise, and patches never change the shipped scenario.

options.label: Variants are full copies of the scenario package
No A/B support; compare separate runs by eye

text: Which computer opponents should the harness pit against each other?

options.label: Today's computer player on every side, with a per-faction AI profile (weights) that a variant can change
options.rationale: Separates rule balance from AI quality and lets us test whether the Southern weakness is the AI or the board.

options.label: Also a random-legal player as a baseline (plan.md section 12.2)
Today's computer player only, no profiles

text: Where should the harness report be read?

options.label: A generated HTML page in build/sim/ next to summary.json and games.csv
options.rationale: Readable in the morning without tools; the JSON and CSV feed any deeper analysis.

options.label: Console summary and JSON only
A developer screen inside the game

text: Where should the line between data and code sit?

options.label: Parameters in data; named rule modules in code, selected by data, each with its own spec rules and tests
options.rationale: Honours the north star and the 'no premature abstraction' principle; matches Wesnoth and Ludii, and keeps rules testable (Revision 6 section 1.6).

options.label: Rules as data: formulas, triggers, and effect scripts in JSON
Keep Milestone 3 mechanics in code; move things to data only when a second game mode needs them

text: How should the Spain game's data files be laid out?

options.label: One file per scenario: src/main/scenarios/spain-1936-07-31/scenario.json plays the role of spain-civil-war-scenario.json, gaining a rules section (modules, unit types, combat, resources, weather, AI, calendar); split into a shared game-mode file when a second start date is planned
options.rationale: One file holds everything, as the owner expects, with no loader change; the split later is mechanical because the loader composes files into one Scenario.

options.label: Split now: src/main/modes/spain-civil-war/mode.json (rules and board, the owner's file) shared by starts/1936-07-31.json and later 1937 and 1938 starts
Rename to the owner's literal name, src/main/scenarios/spain-civil-war/spain-civil-war-scenario.json (the loader glob for */scenario.json changes)
One scenario file that extends a shared rules file and overrides parts of it

text: Should computer-player weights move into the scenario data?

options.label: Yes: named AI profiles in data, one per faction, holding today's computerWeights, offensiveWeights, stakeWeights, and victoryAlarm numbers; the strategy logic stays in code
options.rationale: They are already plain numbers; in data the harness can A/B them per faction, as Paradox scripts AI weights.

options.label: Yes, and let data choose among several coded strategies per faction
No: keep them as code constants

text: How should unit special effects (artillery roll bonus, bombing a town) be expressed?

options.label: Data names an effect kind from a coded list and gives its numbers, for example roll-bonus-per-points with per 3, bonus 1
options.rationale: The Wesnoth pattern: each kind is tested once and reused by every era.

options.label: Free-form formulas in data
Code per unit type

text: How much should Milestone 3 design for future eras?

options.label: Check each new module on paper against one other era (WW1 is the closest), and build nothing for other eras yet
options.rationale: Catches Spain-only assumptions cheaply while the owner says other game types come later.

options.label: Build a small second test scenario in another era to prove the engine
Design only for Spain; generalise when a second era starts

text: Should the turn calendar (start date and 14-day turns) become scenario data now?

options.label: Yes: a calendar block with start date and turn length in days, shown on the turn banner
options.rationale: Weather by month needs a date, and other eras use other turn lengths.

options.label: Only if the weather idea is accepted
No: keep turns numbered without dates

text: How should the new rules be named in scenario data?

options.label: ruleset m3-modular plus a rules object that picks one named module per area (dice, economy, recruitment, weather, supply, movement, partition); m2-strength kept as a preset
options.rationale: Avoids one id per combination, lets a scenario take only what it needs, and lets the harness compare m2 and m3 rules.

options.label: A single new id, m3-economy, that includes every Milestone 3 rule
One ruleset id per combination of rules

text: How should the scenario spec version change?

options.label: Bump to spec version 2, migrate both packages (Spain, tiny-front) in one commit, and drop version 1
options.rationale: Only two packages and no saved games exist, so keeping version 1 would be cost without users.

options.label: Bump to version 2 and keep loading version 1 packages
Stay on version 1 and add only optional fields

text: Should Milestone 3 add Diplomacy-style support orders (Revision 5 OD-9)?

options.label: Not in Milestone 3: measure the freeze rate with recruitment and the other new rules through the harness first, then decide
options.rationale: Combined attacks from several origins (M17) already give most of what a support does; a second order type adds rules and UI.

options.label: Yes, add support orders in Milestone 3
Drop support orders for good

text: What balance targets should Milestone 3 aim at?

options.label: Over 1000 games: freeze rate at or under 20 percent, and every faction winning at least 20 percent of decided games; report misses to the owner rather than tuning in a loop
options.rationale: Gives the harness a stated target, which simulation balancing needs, without forcing equal shares on a historical asymmetry; at 1000 games a share is known to about +/- 3 points.

options.label: Equal shares: each faction 25 to 42 percent of decided games
No targets; keep reporting numbers only (as P3 in Milestone 2)
